key_insight: Population-based reference equations contextualize neurodegeneration blood biomarkers using age, sex, body-mass index, and renal function to generate individualized expected concentrations, percentiles, and Z-scores.
clinical_relevance: This neurodegeneration study—not AI cancer drug discovery—supports research into more consistent biomarker interpretation rather than establishing standalone diagnostic thresholds.
method: Analyzed plasma from cognitively unimpaired participants in two French population-based cohorts.
Used generalized additive models to derive reference equations for NfL, GFAP, p-tau181, amyloid-β40, amyloid-β42, and biomarker ratios.
Applied Z-scores to clinical cohorts and developed NfL cross-calibration equations across analytical methods and sample matrices.
evidence_signal: Reference samples included 5,123 participants for amyloid biomarkers and p-tau181 and 5,122 for NfL and GFAP; disease-associated profiles were preserved, and NfL cross-calibration agreement exceeded an intraclass correlation coefficient of 0.90.
watch_item: The cross-sectional French reference cohorts do not establish longitudinal predictive performance or generalizability to other populations.
paper_title: Population-based reference equations and Z-scores for blood biomarkers of neurodegenerative diseases
